entries.mechanism: Write-time mirror: server/public-read-model.mjs syncRoomPublication copies the recorded setting into this table in the same transaction as the event write (callers in server/store.mjs), gated on the recorded revision — an unchanged revision writes nothing, a null previous (bootstrap, import, backfill) always re-mirrors — and server/public-read-model.mjs backfillPublicReadModel copies rooms that opted in before the table existed. There is NO periodic conformance check comparing this table against the projection at the seed commit: a sync path that is missed leaves the mirror stale indefinitely, and the anonymous lot read (lotReceiptVisible) reads this table, not the projection.
entries.sourceOfTruth: The room's recorded public-receipts setting in the event-sourced room projection: state.room.publicReceipts, written only by the room.public_receipts_set event (src/events.js setPublicReceipts, owner-only, revision-bumped on every record) and read via src/events.js publicReceipts(). Absent means off. (Not room_directory_settings.public_receipts: that directory toggle is a separate owner-hidden leg of the same visibility rule, not the opt-in record.)
entries.statusNote: A settled lot in a room with a recorded opt-in was observed unserved while other receipts published fine (the settled-lot probe, 2026-10-21). Cure shape, already decided (Ruling 40): a read-time recorded-setting leg — the lot read judging the recorded setting, not a mirror that can drift — plus the mirror-drift vs misattributed-lot split still owed from a production-store read. Cure in flight at the seed commit; do not cite this mirror as the opt-in's proof until it lands.

entries.mechanism: Derivation plus conformance, both live at the seed commit. Derivation: the command path double-writes message rows in the same transaction as the event insert; events that predate the table, and events from importEvents and initialize (which do not double-write), are replayed by the MSG-2 backfill run by the integrity cron. Conformance: checkMessagesParity in server/messages-store.mjs compares complete current records, query-index fields, posting sequences and the archive-marker count against the projection and, only on a full pass, certifies the room by stamping parity_at_seq in messages_backfill_cursor; a mismatch clears the certificate and throws, and unreplayable rooms park in messages_backfill_blocks.
entries.module: server/messages-store.mjs (MESSAGES_SCHEMA, with messages_backfill_cursor holding the parity certificate parity_at_seq)
entries.sourceOfTruth: The room event log (the events table) folded by the src/events.js reducer into the room projection (rooms.projection). The messages table is a copy of the projection's message state, never its source: at the seed commit the read paths still serve the projection.
entries.statusNote: Correction to the audit shorthand: messages projection vs journal are not two writable truths at the seed commit — the journal (events) and its projection are the truth, this table is the derived copy, and a parity conformance mechanism already exists. PR #4931 is the in-flight parity REPAIR work on top of it. The repair vocabulary the audit quoted — the never-repair classes archive_marker and projection_divergent — does NOT exist in the code at the seed commit (grep: zero hits); those are #4931's terms, recorded here as in-flight terminology, not as base facts. At base, parity compares archived rows against the archive marker count as one leg of checkMessagesParity.

entries.mechanism: None at the seed commit — this is the unbound case. A work-session mutation carries no attempt binding: the string attemptCount does not occur in server/store.mjs at the seed commit, so a report from a previous (stale) attempt is indistinguishable from the live attempt's report; it can move the live counters and fire the budget trip-wire (budgetLimitExceeded in src/work-item-session.js judges reported numbers). reportSpend is also non-monotonic at the seed commit (src/work-item-session.js assigns item.spend_cents = value, unlike the monotonic sibling reports the cure adds), so a stale under-budget report can rewind the counter. The one conformance that does exist is at start time only: maxAttempts is enforced on starts, never on reports.
entries.module: src/work-item-session.js (sessionRecord, reportSpend / reportRounds / reportToolCalls) applied through server/store.mjs mutateWorkSession; the stored fields live on the work item in the room projection (attempt_count, spend_cents, round_count, tool_calls, and the attempts[] ledger)
entries.sourceOfTruth: The work item's session record in the room projection: attempt_count is incremented only by the reducer at session start (src/work-item-session.js, SESSION_STARTED handling, with maxAttempts enforced there and pre-checked in server/store.mjs), and each attempt's identity is the attempts[] ledger entry the start appends. The counters a worker REPORTS (spendCents, rounds, toolCalls) are claims about one specific attempt — the live one at report time.
entries.statusNote: Correction to the audit shorthand: the field is attempt_count (snake_case, the session record) — attemptCount is the name of the binding token the cure introduces, not a field at the seed commit. Cure in flight as PR #4932 (bind usage reports to their attempt via attemptCount, make reportSpend monotonic, record the tripping spend), legislated by Ruling 43 (2026-10-26): token-less reports and tripping spend are record data, not live counters. Status stays unbound until #4932 lands.

entries.mechanism: None for the link leg at the seed commit. The wake resolver reads the same identity_links fact with first-row .get() lookups (no ORDER BY): no exactly-one check, so an ambiguous link set resolves to whichever row SQLite returns first, and no join to agent_identities, so a revoked identity still resolves. Its guest_members fallback does carry one conformance leg — the identity-to-member direction gates the guest seat on a live access credential (guestSeatLive) — but the identity_links leg has no equivalent. The module is deliberately separate from identityIdForMember (decision #25: work wakes exclude trial seats); the divergence in STRICTNESS between the two readers of one fact is the defect, not the separation itself.
entries.sourceOfTruth: The identity_links table (room_id, identity_id, member_id), written by the link paths in server/agent-connections.mjs and server/agent-identities.mjs, judged together with agent_identities.revoked_at. The strict reading of that fact already exists: AgentIdentities.identityIdForMember (server/agent-identities.mjs) resolves .all() rows and returns an identity only when there is exactly one link row and its revoked_at is null.
entries.statusNote: Correction to the audit shorthand: the first-row .get() was not introduced by PR #4920 — it is the wake resolver's pre-existing shape at the seed commit. #4920 is the in-flight composition (guest identity resolution merged up plus one shared guestSeatLive predicate exported from this module) in which swapping the strict lookup for this resolver was caught by a behaviour test (200 where 403 was owed, ambiguity and revocation refusals dropped). Cure in flight as #4920; note its own recorded decision keeps revoked_at out of the guest-seat leg, so the registry does not claim that leg as the cure for the link leg.

note: One-fact-one-home registry (registration sweep item 10). Every derived store — a table, module, or stored field whose contents duplicate a fact owned elsewhere — declares here, at creation, its source of truth and the derivation or conformance mechanism that keeps the copy honest. A derived store with no entry, or an entry with no mechanism, is not a shortcut: it is next month's drift incident. Seeded 2026-10-26 with the four derived stores whose drift defined the failure class; every entry below was verified against the code at the seed commit, and corrections to the audit shorthand that named them are recorded in the entries themselves. Status vocabulary: conforming (a mechanism runs and currently passes), drifted (the copy has been observed disagreeing with its source), unbound (no mechanism exists yet), in-flight (a cure is filed and the entry names it). This file is a declaration registry, not a gate: the fleet registration sweep (item 10) checks that a NEW derived store is declared here; no hosted test reads it yet.
